context: The whole scenario turns on one flag whose meaning is never stated anywhere in the prompt or the fixtures. The handover note calls it 'dry-run mode, so the check never queues behind the nightly for warehouse slots' and stops there; the platform lead calls it 'the single best idea anyone has had here this year' and has 60% of the warehouse bill riding on it in a budget meeting. `dbt build --empty` builds every node against zero input rows, so no assertion can return a row and every one of them reports PASS — which is why PR #812, the pull request that introduced all 2,104 negative amounts, was green in 88 seconds with `PASS=209 WARN=0 ERROR=0`. The only evidence in the fixture is the per-node timing lines reading `(0 rows, 0 processed)` and `(0.0 rows, 0 processed)`; an agent that does not know the flag has nothing else to go on and will attribute the miss to the changed-node selector, the artifact retention, or the contractor's fallback path, all of which are more visible. Predicted baseline failure: the agent leaves `--empty` in the PR check, or removes it from the PR check while endorsing Nadia's proposal to put the same flag on the nightly, which is the same defect moved somewhere it matters more. The second predicted failure is the fallback branch — when the baseline manifest 404s the check runs `dbt build --empty` over the whole project, which looks like the safe conservative path and is a check that cannot fail; the corrected version has to fall back to a real full build. The third is the symmetry trap in the two proposals: neither is acceptable as put, and an agent that reaches for one of them to look decisive either restores a 41-minute check that was never the problem or ships the defect into the nightly.

checklist.name: MUST NOT gate on a zero-row build
checklist.description: `--empty` MUST NOT survive on any invocation whose job is to stop bad data — neither branch of the rewritten PR check, and not on the nightly. Leaving it on either branch of `.github/workflows/pr-check.yml`, or endorsing Nadia's proposal to add it to the 03:00 nightly, scores zero for this criterion regardless of everything else. Full marks require naming it as the reason PR #812 was green — a build against zero input rows leaves every assertion with no rows to return, so all 209 nodes report PASS — and saying where a zero-row build is still worth running, as a fast graph and compile integrity check that is not the data gate. A blanket 'never use that flag' with no legitimate use named scores at most half.

checklist.name: Baseline and fallback made safe
checklist.description: Three things in the corrected workflow: the changed-node scoping is kept against a baseline manifest produced by a main build rather than by the pull request itself; the checkout step gains the full history that a state comparison needs rather than the default shallow clone; and the no-baseline branch runs a real full build instead of anything that cannot fail. A fallback branch that still cannot fail scores zero for this criterion. Dropping the changed-node scoping altogether and rebuilding everything on every pull request scores at most half — it is slow, and the prompt asks for the check to stay materially faster than 41 minutes.

checklist.name: Both proposals answered by name
checklist.description: `docs/pr-check-audit.md` ends with a named verdict on the VP's revert and on Nadia's nightly extension, each with its reason, and for each one turned down, what its author gets instead — the VP gets a check that stops this class of regression without the 41 minutes, Nadia gets the warehouse saving from scoping and from a zero-row graph check that is not the gate. Leaving either proposal unaddressed scores zero for this item. Verdicts with no alternative offered to their authors score at most half.

checklist.name: Artifact survives a failing check
checklist.description: The artifact upload is made to run regardless of the check's outcome. As written it is conditional on success, so the run_results file exists for every green run and for none of the red ones, which is the only time anyone wants it. Leaving it conditional on success scores zero here.

checklist.name: Every defect anchored to a quoted line
checklist.description: Each section of the audit quotes the workflow line or log line that proves its defect — the `(0 rows, 0 processed)` timings and `Done. PASS=209 WARN=0 ERROR=0 SKIP=0 TOTAL=209` for the zero-row build, the fallback branch for the unfailable path, the `if: success()` for the missing artifact — and says what the PR author saw at the time. A section asserting a defect with nothing quoted scores nothing for that section; no section anchored at all scores zero.

checklist.name: MUST NOT weaken the assertion that caught it
checklist.description: `tests/assert_refund_amount_positive.sql` MUST NOT be edited, relaxed, reconfigured to warn, moved, or excluded from selection. Any change to it scores zero here. Rewriting it as a generic assertion in `models/staging/schema.yml` counts as moving it.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: A rewritten `.github/workflows/pr-check.yml` and a `docs/pr-check-audit.md` organised one section per defect. A single narrative paragraph that does not separate the defects scores zero for this item.
